note: Every page of both fixtures is rastered for a human who did not build this family. It matters more than usual here: these two forms cannot be caption-checked from their own text stream, so a reviewer reading the paper is the check that a value sits under the heading it belongs to.
whatToLookAt: JDF 2371 sections A, B, C and 2, and JDF 2374 sections A, B, C and 2: confirm the county, case number, defendant name, birth date, mailing address, city/state/zip, phone and e-mail each sit under the heading they belong to. Both forms give the street its own line and the city, state and zip theirs, and the packet writes them that way: the town and the zip should appear once on the page, not twice.
JDF 2371 section 2: the interpreter question unanswered, the language line blank, and neither in-person nor virtual ticked.

JDF 2371 section 3: the case number appearing on the District or County Court line as well as in the caption — Colorado wires those two to one field — every agency box unticked apart from the Colorado Bureau of Investigation box the form marks required, and every agency name, address and file number blank.
JDF 2371 section 4: the three offence-class boxes unticked, the offence lines blank, and the drug and psilocybin questions unanswered.
JDF 2371 section 7 and section 8: no service date, no method, no recipient, no signature, no date, the printed name line blank, and the counsel block blank.
JDF 2374 section 3: all four court findings unticked and the other-findings box empty. This is the one to look at hardest — a tick there would be the packet making the judge's finding for them.
JDF 2374 section 4 and the signature block: the agency name, file number and arrest number blank, the other-orders box blank, the signature and date blank, and neither Judge nor Magistrate ticked.
